guide.wayaround.assembly.1: Place a Water Wheel Support attached to a structure.
guide.wayaround.assembly.2: Install the Water Wheel Body on the support. The body may sit close to construction; reserve clearance mainly for the boards' path.
guide.wayaround.assembly.3: Hold a Water Wheel Plate, aim directly at the hexagonal frame and click to fit it at that exact point.
guide.wayaround.assembly.4: With an empty hand, click a loose board to rotate it in small steps. Shift + click removes it.
guide.wayaround.assembly.5: Use any item recognized as a nail to lock the board through its mounting hole. An empty hand removes the nail again.
guide.wayaround.assembly.6: Distribute several boards around the wheel. A balanced, unobstructed and evenly covered assembly rotates far more smoothly.
guide.wayaround.assembly.more: Sneak and use the manual to open the diagnostics section.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.1: Poor mass distribution makes the wheel seek its own balance point and oscillate.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.2: A large empty angular gap creates irregular impulses and poor rotation.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.3: If any board hits a solid block during a revolution, the assembly jams. Construction may surround the body itself.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.4: Still or chaotic water produces no mechanical power. The wheel needs a coherent current.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.5: Wood and nails wear out. Creaking and visible cracks mean it is time to disassemble, inspect and replace parts.
guide.wayaround.assembly.7: Connect a Mechanical Shaft along the wheel axle. Use a Mechanical Gearbox to turn or split rotation into other directions, then carry the network to the generator.
guide.wayaround.assembly.diagnostics.6: Deep cracks and splitting wood mean structural failure is imminent. Remove the wheel from load or current to halt the failure progression.
